title: IHateLovePDF: Client-Side PDF Toolkit
tagline: Client-side PDF suite focused on privacy and speed.
description: Client-side tool to split, merge, compress, edit, and decrypt PDF files directly in your browser. All file processing stays local, so your documents never touch a remote server.
problem: Most online PDF converters force strict upload limits and store private documents on external servers.
solution: I used WebAssembly and Web Workers to process PDF binaries right inside browser memory, keeping user data private and operations fast.
key_features: Zero file uploads with purely in-browser processing
WebAssembly-based local PDF compression engine
Drag and drop visual page reordering and rotation
Web Workers running heavy operations off the main thread

title: Hospital Management System
tagline: Clinical workflow and electronic patient record system.
description: Full-stack healthcare app built to handle doctor appointments, patient history (EMR), bed tracking, and pharmacy invoices without scheduling conflicts.
problem: Paper logs and basic spreadsheets often cause overlapping appointments and fragmented patient histories during busy clinic hours.
solution: Built an Express and PostgreSQL backend using Prisma atomic transactions with row locks, guaranteeing conflict-free scheduling even during concurrent bookings.
key_features: Conflict-free appointment booking with database row locks
Organized electronic medical record timelines for each patient
Live ward availability and bed allocation board
Role-based permissions for doctors, staff, and admin

title: ZyMeal: Real-Time Food Ordering
tagline: Food delivery platform with live order updates and clean API design.
description: Food ordering web app with live kitchen tracking, JWT-based user roles, and a fast checkout flow.
problem: Food apps often slow down during dinner rushes, leaving customers and restaurants guessing about order status.
solution: Built a Node.js REST API with Socket.io channels for instant status updates between kitchen staff and diners, validating all inputs with Zod schemas.
key_features: Live order tracking via Socket.io WebSocket channels
Dedicated interfaces for customers, kitchens, and admins
Strict request payload validation using Zod
Automated subtotal calculations and checkout flow

title: GitFC: EA FC Card Generator
tagline: Turn your GitHub profile stats into collectible EA FC cards.
description: Fun web app that pulls your public GitHub activity using GraphQL and scores your contributions into an EA FC style player card you can download.
problem: GitHub profile stats are mostly numbers and commit squares, which makes celebrating milestones a bit dry to share.
solution: Wrote an algorithm that translates commit volume, stars, and PRs into realistic player attributes (PAC, SHO, PAS, DRI, DEF, PHY) with high-res PNG downloads.
key_features: Single GraphQL query to fetch complete yearly contributions
Balanced 0-99 scoring formula mapped to developer metrics
Multiple card themes including TOTY, Gold, and Icon editions
One-click high resolution PNG export rendered in the browser

title: SwipeRide: Real-Time Ride Sharing API
tagline: Real-time driver dispatch and ride matching backend.
description: Ride-sharing API built with Node.js, Express, MongoDB, and Redis. It handles live driver location tracking, fare estimates, and fast pickup matching with dynamic radius expansion.
problem: Constantly recalculating nearest drivers for active ride requests creates heavy database reads that slow down typical query setups.
solution: Implemented MongoDB 2DSphere indexes to run radius searches, cached driver coordinates in Redis for instant lookups, and broadcasted ride status changes over Socket.io.
key_features: Geospatial driver lookup using MongoDB 2DSphere indexes
Sub-5ms driver coordinate reads using Redis in-memory storage
Automatic search radius expansion when nearby drivers are scarce
Real-time trip updates sent over WebSockets
